integrity: The proof uses the exact high-complexity mass comparison and master bad-set upper bound from arXiv:2609.13513 together with the theorem that the universal-semimeasure tail dominates every computable decreasing-to-zero function from arXiv:2608.27098. The conditional estimate is obtained only by division and a quantified little-o argument; the four regimes are then specialized using the source's own series estimates.
scientific_limitations: The result is a normalized conditional consequence of existing absolute universal-measure bounds and the companion tail lemma. It does not sharpen the numerator estimates, does not provide effective onset thresholds, and does not claim sharp conditional constants or exponents.
title: Conditioning on high complexity preserves probabilistic-randomness decay regimes
